sentenceSets.sentence: A small cabal of loyalists controlled access to the director, screening all requests for audiences.

answerChoices.reasoning: A clique is an exclusive social circle defined by whom it shuts out socially, while this group holds a lever of institutional power by deciding who may reach the director.
A committee is formally constituted with an announced mandate, but these loyalists screen requests informally on the director's behalf.
A coalition is an open alliance between parties with distinct interests, whereas these are loyalists bound to one man and working quietly around him.
An entourage merely accompanies an important person, while this group actively controls who gets through to him.
A congregation gathers for worship and has no role in screening petitions to an office holder.
A jury is empaneled to decide a case, not to regulate access to a director.
A delegation is sent to represent others elsewhere, the opposite of a group stationed around the director to filter arrivals.
A workforce is the whole body of employees, not the small circle the sentence says guarded the director.
A throng is a large disorganized crowd, contradicting the sentence's emphasis on a small controlling group.
A menagerie is a collection of animals and cannot screen requests for audiences.
An electorate is the whole voting public, which is neither small nor positioned to guard one official's door.

sentenceSets.sentence: Historians have long argued over whether a genuine cabal engineered the coup or whether the colonels simply moved at the same moment out of panic.

answerChoices.reasoning: A conspiracy is the secret plan itself, but the sentence asks whether a group of plotters existed as against colonels acting independently, which makes the question one of persons rather than schemes.
A faction is an openly identifiable wing within a larger body, while the historians' dispute turns on whether anything was secretly organized at all.
A junta is the military government that rules after a seizure of power, whereas the sentence concerns whoever might have planned the coup beforehand.
A mutiny is the act of revolt, not a body of people who could be said to have engineered it.
A tribunal judges cases after the fact and could not have engineered the coup.
A regiment is a formal military unit whose existence no historian would dispute, unlike the hidden group in question.
An assembly meets publicly and on the record, which is at odds with something historians can only argue about the existence of.
A bureaucracy is the standing administrative apparatus, not a hidden group that might have coordinated the colonels.
The populace is the general public, which could not have secretly engineered anything.
An anniversary is a date, not an agent capable of engineering a coup.
A referendum is a public vote, the opposite of the secret coordination the historians debate.

sentenceSets.sentence: He was convinced that a cabal within the department was feeding his rivals the minutes of every meeting he attended.

answerChoices.reasoning: A mole is a single planted informant, while the sentence's suspicion is of a group operating together inside the department.
A rumor is talk that circulates, not something capable of handing his rivals the actual minutes of meetings.
A supervisor is one identifiable superior, whereas his conviction is about a hidden set of colleagues acting in concert.
A network is a neutral web of connections that may serve any purpose, and the sentence describes a group he believes is secretly working against him.
A ledger is a record book and cannot feed anything to anyone.
A union is an open representative body with declared membership, unlike a hidden group leaking his meeting notes.
A vendetta is a feud, an activity rather than the set of people he believes is passing documents along.
A protocol is a rule of procedure and has no capacity to leak minutes to rivals.
A custodian maintains a building and does not fit a suspicion about leaked meeting records.
A holiday is a period of time and cannot feed minutes to anyone.
A printer is a machine, not a group within the department conspiring against him.
